payload.decision_topic: Audition the 12 Shepard drones (Stage 1 MINIMUM-ILLUSION) — does the Gaussian stack read as ONE Shepard tone per pitch class?
payload.subject: Audition the 12-drone Stage-1 Shepard sample library
payload.rationale:
Catch-up: GSL+Shepard Phase 3 source-two just landed. The two stewards rendezvoused in this batch: Shepard wrote shepard_synth.py with a convenience wrapper for me, I wrote the adapter, and the full 12-drone library is on disk under [Projects/Generative Sample Libraries/shepard-instrument/](open:Projects/Generative Sample Libraries/shepard-instrument/?reveal). Load [shepard_instrument.sfz](open:Projects/Generative Sample Libraries/shepard-instrument/shepard_instrument.sfz) in sforzando — every MIDI note plays its pitch-class drone, 7-octave Gaussian stack centered at C4.

This is a Stage-1 sensory deliverable; per the audition rule the full batch cannot proceed past 'rendered' to 'shipped' without your ear. Two questions only listening can answer:

1. **COHERENT-STACK** — does the 7-octave Gaussian stack sound like one Shepard tone per drone, or seven distinct octaves stacked? If it splits into seven, sigma=1.0 octave may be too wide (we hear discrete partials) and a tighter sigma (~0.6-0.8) would fuse them. That would be a Shepard-side parameter tweak, not a GSL change.
2. **CLASS-IDENTITY** — when you play adjacent pitch classes (C then C#, F then F#), do they read as distinct drones, or as the same drone in slight detune? If the latter, the centroid+sigma combo may be smearing pitch-class identity and Stage 1's parameter choices need revision before Stage 2 adds motion on top.

Three response shapes worth pre-naming so the click means something concrete:
- APPROVE — both pass; Stage 1 of GSL+Shepard is shipped. Next cycle moves to Phase 3 source three OR Phase 4 multi-destination prep.
- TWEAK-PARAMS — one or both fail in a way that points at sigma/centroid; I post a coordination ask to Shepard naming what I heard and Shepard runs a parameter sweep cycle.
- REJECT — Stage 1 is wrong-shaped (not a parameter issue, a structural one); we reconsider TWELVE-DRONES or the Stage 1 spec itself.
payload.decision_needed: Listen to the 12 drones in sforzando. Does the Stage-1 illusion read?

options.label: APPROVE — both questions pass. Stage 1 of GSL+Shepard is shipped.
TWEAK-PARAMS — sigma or centroid is off; I'll coordinate a parameter sweep with the Shepard steward.
REJECT — Stage 1 is structurally wrong; reconsider TWELVE-DRONES or the spec.

payload.rationale:
Quick catch-up: I'm the dual-wavetable additive synthesis project — Wavetable A controls per-partial amplitudes, Wavetable B controls per-partial frequency deviations in cents, a flat horizontal Wavetable-B line IS the harmonic series and any curve away from it is the inharmonicity signature of some material. Cycle 1 asked where to start; you granted PROTOTYPE-IN-FAUST. This cycle shipped that prototype: 32 partials, 4 amplitude presets, 5 inharmonicity curves (flat, piano B-coefficient, Bessel zeros, stochastic scatter, inverse), a B-Depth knob, and a settling-piano envelope.

This is a sensory deliverable so the audition gate applies before I commit any more labor. The smallest unit that exercises every parameter is a single held note swept through the 5 Wavetable-B presets at three B-Depth levels (0 / 1 / 2) and two settle times (0.3 s / 3 s). The [README](obsidian://open?vault=The%20Palace&file=Projects/Inharmonic%20Wavetable%20Synthesis/faust-prototype/README.md) lays this out as a five-pass checklist — open the .dsp in [faustide.grame.fr](https://faustide.grame.fr/), hit play, run the checklist. About 4 minutes of listening.

The architectural claim under test: each Wavetable-B preset should land in a recognizably different family of physical objects (string family / bell family / wood-block family / impossible-material) even though Wavetable A barely changes. If yes, the dual-wavetable concept is verified and I move on to multi-frame WT-B scanning or FFT-driven WT-A or per-partial pan. If no, I tune the curves before going further.

options.label: ARCHITECTURE-VERIFIED — the five passes do what the spec promises; greenlight the next phase and I'll come back with a fork between multi-frame WT-B, FFT-driven WT-A, and Wavetable-C.
TUNE-CURVES — the right idea but one or more curves don't land. Name which preset(s) feel off and I'll re-audition before moving on.
WRONG-AUDITION-UNIT — five-pass single-note isn't the right test. Propose what would actually convince you (a chord? a slow B-Depth LFO sweep? side-by-side with a real piano sample?).
COULDN'T-RUN-IT — Faust web IDE failed, .dsp didn't compile, or the controls didn't behave. Paste what you saw and I'll fix the prototype.

payload.decision_topic: Does the Stage 1 MINIMUM-ILLUSION drone read as one pitch class, not seven sines?
payload.rationale:
Catch-up: Stage 1 just shipped as [shepard_synth.py](open:Projects/Shepard%20Tone%20Synthesizer/shepard_synth.py?reveal) — seven sines (C1..C7 for a C drone) weighted by a Gaussian envelope in log2(Hz) centered at C4. No motion. The claim Stage 1 is making is that octave equivalence is strong enough to fuse seven simultaneous octave-related sines into one perceived pitch class — and that this fusion is the perceptual axiom Stage 2 (ASCENT-FIRST) will lean on. If the drone reads as seven separate sines instead of one note, the whole staged arc rests on sand.

The sprout-stage rule is to audition the smallest unit that exercises every parameter before committing to a full batch — twelve drones, one per pitch class, is the natural batch (it also satisfies the GSL TWELVE-DRONES grant). I have rendered two audition drones so you can judge with one click: [Stage 1 C drone](open:Projects/Shepard%20Tone%20Synthesizer/proofs/stage1_drone_C.wav) and [Stage 1 F♯ drone](open:Projects/Shepard%20Tone%20Synthesizer/proofs/stage1_drone_F-sharp.wav). I picked C and F♯ because they are a tritone apart — maximum pitch-class distance, the most demanding case for the envelope to keep them sounding 'the same kind of thing.'

What to listen for: (a) does each drone read as a single pitch class, not as a chord of separate sines? (b) is the registration (the 'where in the spectrum') consistent between C and F♯, or does one feel higher/lower than the other in a way that breaks the static-drone framing? (c) any audible discontinuities, beating, or buzz that suggest the envelope shape is wrong? How would you like to proceed?

options.label: APPROVE-RENDER-TWELVE — drone reads as one pitch class; render the full chromatic twelve at 48 kHz / 4 s and hand them to the GSL steward for TWELVE-DRONES.
ADJUST-ENVELOPE — close, but the envelope width (sigma=1.0 octave) or centroid (C4) needs tuning; name what is off and I re-audition with adjusted params before rendering the batch.
ADJUST-STACK — the seven-octave range (C1..C7) needs revisiting; e.g. drop C1/C7 if they're inaudible noise, or extend to C0/C8 if the bright zone feels truncated.

REJECT-RECIPE — the drone does not read as one pitch class at all; Stage 1 needs a different recipe (e.g. raised-cosine instead of Gaussian, or a literal bandpass post-sum instead of per-voice weighting).

payload.rationale: The Faust .dsp is drafted but I have not yet compiled or rendered it — and the demo that proves whether the Kuramoto coupling is actually audible is a sensory deliverable that needs a gate before I commit labor to the full render batch. The cleanest demo is a slow K-sweep on a fixed population, recorded as audio so we can hear the synchronization phase transition emerge. Three audition framings, each with a different teaching shape: (a) K sweep alone at a fixed pitch, (b) K sweep + frequency sweep so the pitch domain is exercised too, (c) a discrete A/B of K=0 vs K=0.5 vs K=1.5 (three short clips, no sweep). The K-sweep is the most dramatic; the A/B is the most legible; the combined sweep is the most musically interesting but the hardest to hear cleanly. There is also an honest fourth path: compile the .dsp first to surface any Faust errors before deciding the demo shape.

options.label: K-SWEEP — 30s render, fixed 220Hz, K linear 0→1; the canonical synchronization-phase-transition demo.
DUAL-SWEEP — 30s render, K linear 0→1 alongside a slow pitch glide; tests both axes at once.
AB-CLIPS — three 10s clips at K=0 / K=0.5 / K=1.5; cleanest pedagogical comparison.
COMPILE-FIRST — run Faust compile next cycle to catch syntax errors before picking a demo.

payload.decision_topic: Where does the optical-acoustic bridge go next, now that birefringence is proven?
payload.rationale:
Re-grounding: I'm the synthesizer that maps phonon modes of crystals into timbre. Forward vector: make the *optical* properties of crystals audible. Cycle 2 just shipped the ruby birefringence proof — five WAVs at [birefringence-proof/](obsidian://open?vault=The%20Palace&file=Projects/Crystal%20Synthesizer/birefringence-proof/README.md), with the predicted 8.80 Hz beat empirically confirmed at 8.89 Hz. One optical analogy is now an audible artifact. The bridge has two more legs.

Four next moves, each picking up a different half-built path. **DISPERSION-FILTER** would build Option 3 from my body — a frequency-dependent delay filter where each partial of a broadband click arrives at a different time, derived from a phonon dispersion curve $\omega(k) = 2\sqrt{K/m}|\sin(ka/2)|$. This is the time-domain partner to birefringence's frequency-domain proof, and the one that most differentiates me from any other modal synth. The existing [crystal_0_dispersion_demo.wav](open:Crystal%20Audio/crystal_0_dispersion_demo.wav) is a one-shot, not a filter. **BIREFRINGENCE-FAMILY** would do the same proof I just did for ruby on emerald (hexagonal, P6/mcc, 174 phonon branches, ring-breathing mode at r≈1.68) and quartz (P3₁21, 9 modes spanning r=1.00–8.32 including a soft mode). If birefringent beats appear in all three across the trigonal/hexagonal family, the claim graduates from 'ruby is the textbook case' to 'this is a symmetry-class signature.' **PLEOCHROISM-PROOF** would build the third optical analogy: the frequency content of a phonon pulse depending on its propagation direction in the crystal. In ruby that means rendering c-axis vs basal-plane excitations as different starting amplitude weightings on the two mode families — pleochroism heard as the same crystal sounding different when 'viewed' from different directions. Closes all three optical analogies in the body. **SIBLING-FEEDBACK** would loop back to what GSL and GWL surfaced last batch: predict which crystal mode reads as the perceptual pitch for the hexagonal multisample (likely the ring-breathing mode at r=1.68, not the lowest), and propose a physical ordering for GWL's seven-lattice sweep (by mode-density, by symmetry-group containment, or by the Bravais inclusion tree).

I lean DISPERSION-FILTER. The vector names three optical phenomena to make audible (birefringence, dispersion, pleochroism); ruby just covered one; dispersion is the conceptually deepest of the remaining two because it is *time-domain* not frequency-domain — a prism separating arrival times, not pitches. BIREFRINGENCE-FAMILY is tempting as a generalization move but builds breadth on one already-proven idea rather than reaching for the next leg of the bridge. SIBLING-FEEDBACK is reactive and advances my siblings' vectors more than mine.
payload.decision_needed: Which leg of the optical-acoustic bridge do I build next?

options.label: DISPERSION-FILTER — build the phase-dispersion filter (Option 3 from my body); broadband click smeared in time by a phonon dispersion curve. The time-domain partner to today's frequency-domain proof. (recommended)
BIREFRINGENCE-FAMILY — repeat today's proof on emerald and quartz; turn 'ruby is the textbook case' into 'this is a symmetry-class signature.'

PLEOCHROISM-PROOF — render the third optical analogy: same crystal sounding different from different propagation directions (c-axis excitation vs basal-plane excitation reweighting the two mode families).
SIBLING-FEEDBACK — work GSL's strike-tone wrinkle (predict the ring-breathing mode at r=1.68 is the perceptual pitch) and propose a physical ordering for GWL's seven-lattice sweep.
YOU-DECIDE — name a different next move.

payload.steward_recommendation: DISPERSION-FILTER — the optical-acoustic vector names three phenomena; birefringence is done, and dispersion is the conceptually deepest of the two remaining because it lives in the time domain, not the frequency domain. Same physics, different observational projection — and the prism analogy lands hardest when arrival times separate the way wavelengths do.

payload.subject: AUDITION — Crystal Bravais 64-frame wavetable (first listenable proof)
payload.rationale: I rendered the first listenable Crystal Bravais proof and need ears on it before I build anything else. The file is at /Users/loudonstearns/Documents/The Palace/_ops/wavetable-libraries/crystal-bravais/crystal_bravais_ableton.wav — drop it into Ableton's Wavetable (or any single-cycle sampler at 1024 samples/frame) and sweep the position from start to end. It morphs cubic to triclinic: pure 3-partial tone opening, thickening to a dense detuned spectrum (verified: significant partials climb 3 to 63 across the sweep). Caveat: the symmetry-to-timbre mapping is a deliberately simplified first sketch, not rigorous crystallography. Listen FOR whether the sweep reads as one intentional motion rather than a random morph. I'm holding the Serum/CLM writer and all Phase 2 work until you've heard this.
options: accept — sweep reads as intentional; proceed (Serum/CLM writer once a reference WAV lands)
tweak-model — motion's there but the partial recipes need reshaping; tell me which end feels off
try-carry-phase — too tame; build a carry_phase_through variant

payload.steward_recommendation: accept — keep zero_phase_reset; the spectral progression is clean and monotonic. Only reach for carry-phase if it sounds inert.

payload.decision_topic: Source-two work split with the Shepard Tone Synthesizer steward
payload.rationale:
Catch-up: I'm the chat-driven multisampled instrument generator. Phase 3 source one (Crystal Hexagonal) shipped 176 WAVs in cycle 9. You just granted `gsl-steward-017` SECOND-PALACE with the note 'Build the Shepard-Tone synthesizer' — and in the same batch run you enchanted a **Shepard Tone Synthesizer** steward. We share an artifact surface and the natural failure mode is racing the same files. I want to settle the coordination shape before either of us starts.

The forks I see: (1) **GSL drives, Shepard supplies** — I run the Interview, drive renders into `Projects/Generative Sample Libraries/shepard-instrument/`, and ask Shepard via the BBS for the synthesis function or parameter ranges; Shepard's page stays the canonical home for the synthesis design. (2) **Shepard drives, GSL receives** — Shepard ships a `shepard_synth.py` (mirroring `crystal_synth.py`) under its own bundle, and I write a thin adapter (mirroring cycle 8's crystal adapter) and run the Interview against it. (3) **Co-build a small spec first** — neither steward renders this cycle; we exchange one BBS round naming the interface (function signature, parameter set, who owns the SFZ).

My recommendation: **option 2** mirrors the working Crystal pattern exactly (palace page owns the synthesis, GSL owns the multisample adapter + SFZ) and is the lowest-friction shape. Option 3 is the safest if Shepard turns out to be `seed`-stage and underspecified.

options.label: GSL-DRIVES — I run the Interview, drive renders, pull synthesis from Shepard via the BBS.
SHEPARD-DRIVES — Shepard ships shepard_synth.py; I write a thin adapter mirroring the Crystal pattern. (recommended)
SPEC-FIRST — neither steward renders yet; we exchange one BBS round naming the interface first.
YOU-DECIDE — name a different shape.
